elements.evidence: "Each Order Form renews for twelve months"

elements.element: Customer may opt out of renewal on 30 days' notice
elements.evidence: "unless either Party gives 30 days' advance written notice"
"Vendor shall give Customer written notice of each upcoming renewal at least 60 days before renewal."

elements.element: Price increases capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%
elements.evidence: "only by the lesser of the increase in the United States Consumer Price Index ... and three percent"

elements.element: Automatic renewal with non-renewal notice window of no more than 60 days
elements.evidence: "renews for twelve months unless either Party gives 30 days' advance written notice"
"lesser of the increase in the ... Consumer Price Index ... and three percent"

reasons: The redline changes only the notice-window number (180 → 30 days) and adds a single concise sentence supplying the absent 60-day Vendor renewal reminder; all four preferred elements (12-month automatic renewal, 30-day Customer opt-out, 60-day reminder, lesser-of-CPI-and-3% cap) are now express in operative text.
The pre-existing CPI/3% cap and 90-day notice of increase in 8.3 were left untouched, so the fallback ≤5% ceiling is also satisfied and no unrelated commercial term is disturbed.

Note (not a deviation): the 30-day window is drafted mutually, so Vendor may also decline renewal on 30 days' notice; this is a consequence of amending the existing symmetrical mechanic rather than an added exception, and no undefined term or dangling cross-reference is introduced.
